formulas_lead: Every number Typing-Race shows can be reproduced from this page. There are no hidden adjustments: the formulas are written the way the code computes them, and the constants carry the values in force today.
formulas_speed_intro: Speed and accuracy are always shown together, so a fast but careless run cannot pass for a good one.
formulas_spm_body: The primary speed metric, also known as CPM. We count the characters of the text typed correctly and divide by the attempt’s time: on a finished attempt that is the text’s length N, so SPM = 60 · N / T. A wrong keystroke adds no text, so it is not in the speed: it lowers accuracy and costs time. A character erased and typed again counts once. The time runs from the first keystroke to the last and leaves out any moment the tab was not in focus. If the time is not positive, the speed is zero, not infinity.
formulas_wpm_body: A secondary metric, shown for comparison with familiar tables. A “word” is a conventional five strokes. WPM is SPM divided by 5, without rounding.
formulas_accuracy_body: The share of correct character keystrokes among all character keystrokes.
formulas_accuracy_corrected: A wrong keystroke always counts as an error, even when it is corrected with Backspace. Accuracy is read from the keystroke log, not from the final text.
formulas_accuracy_backspace: Backspace is not a character keystroke, so it is in neither the numerator nor the denominator.
formulas_accuracy_empty: An attempt with no character keystrokes has an accuracy of 0, not 100%: nothing to hide, but nothing to be proud of either.
formulas_errors_body: The error count is all character keystrokes minus the correct ones. Each error is recorded against the character that was awaited at that moment; past the end of the text, against the character typed.
formulas_difficulty_intro: A transition is the move from one key to the next. One of its properties is whether the keyboard row changes on the way. That property can be counted in two ways, and the two give different numbers.
formulas_rowa_title: Reading 1. Adjacent pairs that change row
formulas_rowa_body: Take every pair of adjacent letters in the word and count those where the second key’s row differs from the first key’s row.
formulas_rowb_title: Reading 2. Distinct rows the word touches
formulas_rowb_body: Count how many different keyboard rows the word touches in total; the order of the letters does not matter.
formulas_row_example_rows: Rows of the letters: н top, а home, в home, ч bottom, а home, н top, н top, я bottom.
formulas_row_example_a: Reading 1 gives 5: н→а, в→ч, ч→а, а→н, н→я.
formulas_row_example_b: Reading 2 gives 3: the top, home and bottom rows.
formulas_row_counted_body: We count adjacent pairs that change row (reading 1). That is how the code works: the “row change” property belongs to each transition on its own, and a word’s difficulty is built from its transitions.
formulas_row_why: The reason is simple: we care about how the fingers move, not about which rows a word contains. A word that keeps jumping between the top and bottom rows is harder than one that touches the same three rows in a single smooth pass, yet reading 2 scores them the same.
formulas_row_ambiguity: Where the divergence comes from. The example in the product requirements gives rowChanges = 3 for «навчання». Only reading 2 reproduces that number; reading 1 gives 5. The requirements do not say which to count, so we chose reading 1 and say so openly.
formulas_same_finger_body: A separate property of a transition: both letters are typed by the same finger of the same hand. It is the slowest kind of transition. In our frequency lists such transitions are 18.58% for ЙЦУКЕН and 5.80% for QWERTY, which is why transition training matters more in Ukrainian.
formulas_levels_caption: Levels, their speed benchmarks and accuracy floors
formulas_status_in_force: in force for all of Stage 1
formulas_levels_note: The table is read from one config file (packages/curriculum/src/levels/levels.json), so its values change without touching code. The level follows the stage, not the speed: all of Stage 1 and Stage 2 are judged against the Introduction floor, Academy exercises (Stage 3) against the Confident floor, so no gain in speed raises the accuracy floor. The speed benchmarks are informational and gate nothing.
formulas_mastery_body: An exercise is mastered when three test attempts in a row reach at least the level’s accuracy floor. An attempt below the floor resets the count to zero. A practice attempt never counts.
formulas_stage1_body: Stage 1 is complete when every scale is complete, there are at least five attempts, and the mean accuracy of the last five attempts is at least {floor}%.
formulas_speed_gates_body: Speed never gates progression. An attempt slower than every benchmark but at or above the accuracy floor counts toward the Mastery Rule. The one speed limit is the {max} SPM of the section below, five times the table’s highest benchmark: it screens out a program, not a learner.
formulas_by_hand_body: An attempt counts only if its typing looks like a hand’s. Otherwise the result screen says “Not counted: this does not look like typing by hand”: the attempt is kept, but it counts toward no mastery, key unlock, XP, record, day streak or race.
formulas_by_hand_burst: A median interval between character keystrokes under {ms} ms means half the characters arrived almost at once: that is a program or an extension inserting text. The interval runs from character to character, so the repeats of a held Shift or Backspace between them do not shorten it. A median, not a minimum: the odd near-zero interval real hands make (overlapping keys, a word an input method commits whole) does not move it.
formulas_by_hand_fast: A speed above {max} SPM is 25 characters every second for a whole exercise. Barbara Blackburn’s record is about 1,060 SPM, and typing-race sites treat anything above 1,500 characters a minute as certain cheating. The threshold is generous on purpose: wrongly accusing a learner costs more than one inflated number.
formulas_by_hand_insert: Apart from these rules, the typing surface takes no paste, no drop and no single input event carrying several characters at once: one key makes one character.
formulas_iki_body: The time in milliseconds between two adjacent input events. Every rhythm and confidence figure is built from these intervals.
formulas_rhythm_body: The standard deviation of the intervals divided by their mean (the coefficient of variation), turned into a percentage so that 100% is a perfect metronome. Dividing by the mean makes the number comparable between slow and fast typing: 80 ms of jitter is chaos at 120 ms a key and nothing at 600.
formulas_rhythm_eligible: Only intervals between two consecutive correct keystrokes are used. Left out: the delay before the first key, any interval touching a wrong keystroke, a Backspace or an ignored event, and any interval longer than {ms} ms, which is a pause and not typing. The number of discarded pauses is shown beside the figure, so a smooth result cannot hide them.
formulas_rhythm_small: With fewer than two usable intervals, or a mean of zero, the rhythm is shown as 0: a single interval would score a meaningless 100%.
formulas_conf_body: A score for every key and every transition: how accurately and how quickly you have been typing it lately. It is a product of two factors, not a sum, so an element typed accurately but very slowly and one typed fast but wrongly are equally not confident.
formulas_conf_decay: After every attempt in which an element appeared, the four counters (hits, misses, sum of intervals and sum of their squares) are multiplied by λ = 2^(−1/{half}) ≈ 0.933 and the new observations are added. Recent attempts therefore weigh more, and an observation’s weight halves after {half} observations. An element absent from an attempt does not lose weight.
formulas_conf_timing: Timing comes from correct keystrokes only: the interval before a wrong key measures hesitation, which the miss already counts. A mean interval of zero gets the full speed factor.
formulas_conf_unmeasured: Fewer than {min} weighted observations means there is no value, not a value of zero: a key never pressed is not “zero confident”, it is simply unmeasured.
formulas_conf_gates_body: It only chooses what to practise and how much guidance the keyboard shows. Mastery is accuracy alone and speed never gates progression, so the speed factor inside confidence smuggles in no speed requirement.
